name: Question 12
problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2+5\text{i} \\ 1+3\text{i} \\ 4-7\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2+7\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 5 \\ -4 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the vectors v1 and v2 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[3−41],v2=[−2+5i1+3i4−7i],B=[5000270−72] The vectors v1 and v2 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=5 and λ2=2+7i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[3−70−13354−2]
b
[3−15−46314−7]
c
[8−25−413−54−7]
d
[3−2621374−1]
e
[3−25−41314−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[5000270−72], we deduce that the first column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v1 and the second and third columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v2:

P=[3−25−41314−7]
